method_notes: Targeted sweep of Northern Ireland's non-sport >=1,000-capacity major-event estate, closing the gap left by the earlier NI pass (which reached only 3 theatre/concert venues and 1 conference/exhibition venue for the whole nation). POPULATIONS WORKED THROUGH: (1) Visit Belfast business-events venue directory (https://www.visitbelfastbusiness.events/venues/) - CONFIRMED BLOCKED: the page ships only 4 'featured' listings in server HTML and loads the rest from a Simpleview rest_v2 endpoint (/includes/rest_v2/plugins_listings_listings/find/) that returns 403 'Invalid credentials' without a runtime-generated simpleToken; its sitemap.xml contains no /listing/ URLs. WORKED ROUND by (a) rendering the page in a headless browser, which surfaced ~20 listing names (Galgorm, Game of Thrones Studio Tour, Hastings Europa Hotel, Titanic Belfast, Custom House Belfast, Hilton Belfast, Ulster Transport Museum, Stormont Estate, St Comgall's, 2 Royal Avenue, Bullitt Hotel, Dunadry Hotel, W5 Belfast, Ulster Museum, Ten Square Hotel, Ulster Rugby, Belfast Cathedral, Maldron Hotel, Quintin Castle) - all hotels or attractions, none a non-sport >=1,000 event auditorium not already held; and (b) going to the operators, councils, universities and venues' own sites directly. (2) Tourism NI: discovernorthernireland.com/business-events resolves to a travel-trade page with no venue finder (the business-events venue paths the previous pass hit are still dead), but its THEATRES directory (https://discovernorthernireland.com/things-to-do/arts-culture-and-heritage/theatres/) IS server-rendered and enumerates the national theatre estate: Lyric, Grand Opera House, Waterfront Hall, Theatre at the Mill, Market Place Theatre Armagh, Alley Arts Centre Strabane, Strule Arts Centre Omagh, Ardhowen Theatre Enniskillen, Millennium Forum. Only Grand Opera House (1,058), Waterfront/ICC (2,000-2,250) and Millennium Forum (1,000) clear 1,000 - all three already in the census. (3) Belfast City Council: Ulster Hall and ICC Belfast (BWUH Ltd) already held; City Hall, 2 Royal Avenue and the community-centre estate are sub-1,000; the Council's own Licensing Committee papers were used as GRADE_A evidence for Boucher Road Playing Fields. (4) Derry City & Strabane: Guildhall Main Hall evidenced at 400 seated / 600 standing (sub-1,000, excluded); Millennium Forum already held; St Columb's Hall evidenced at 700 seats in current use (sub-1,000, excluded). (5) Armagh City Banbridge & Craigavon, Causeway Coast & Glens, Mid Ulster, Ards & North Down council hire estates fetched - all community centres and town halls, nothing approaching 1,000. (6) Fermanagh & Omagh: Ardhowen and Strule are sub-1,000; Fermanagh Lakeland Forum is a leisure centre, closed for redevelopment. (7) Queen's University Belfast events estate fetched in full: Whitla Hall 1,200 theatre (already held), Elmwood Hall 478, Great Hall 150, Isdell Courtyard 290, Riddel Hall rooms 276 - nothing else clears 1,000. Ulster University's largest lecture theatres are 400. (8) Royal Ulster Agricultural Society: Balmoral Park / Eikon Exhibition Centre already held (enriched here with the official 10,600 sqm figure); its predecessor the King's Hall is added as CLOSED. (9) Major NI entertainment venues via the Wikipedia UK venue list and promoter/venue sites. JUDGEMENT ON THE TRUE NI ESTATE: Northern Ireland genuinely has a small non-sport >=1,000 estate. The honest indoor list is roughly thirteen buildings: The O2 Belfast (11,200), ICC Belfast/Waterfront (2,000-2,250), Ulster Hall (1,850 standing), Sir William Whitla Hall (1,200), The Telegraph Building (1,200), Grand Opera House (1,058), Millennium Forum (1,000), Assembly Buildings Conference Centre (1,000), Eikon Exhibition Centre (10,600 sqm), Green Pastures Ballymena (1,600 auditorium), Whitewell Metropolitan Tabernacle (c.3,000 sanctuary), plus two now-closed buildings, King's Hall and the Titanic Exhibition Centre. Eight of those were already in the census; this workstream adds the remaining five plus three Belfast outdoor major-event sites. CATEGORY-BOUNDARY DECISIONS, stated so the census owner can override them: (a) HOTELS ARE EXCLUDED, because the brief's scope list does not include them and no hotel appears anywhere in the existing 811-venue census; several NI hotels do market 1,000+ conference/banqueting capacity (Hastings Europa c.1,200 gala, Crowne Plaza Belfast up to 1,000, La Mon Hotel up to 1,000) and would materially change the NI conference count if the census owner wants them in. (b) OUTDOOR CONCERT SITES ARE INCLUDED here as OTHER_MAJOR_EVENT_VENUE (Custom House Square, Ormeau Park, Boucher Road Playing Fields) even though the existing census contains no outdoor non-sport venue anywhere in GB - these are demonstrably among NI's largest event sites and omitting them silently would misdescribe the nation; flagged for review. (c) LARGE CHURCH AUDITORIA ARE INCLUDED (Green Pastures Ballymena, Whitewell Metropolitan Tabernacle) because they are the only non-sport auditoria over 1,000 seats in their districts; both are flagged, and Whitewell carries a null capacity because the only figure found is a 2010 third-party description. NOT ESTABLISHED / STILL OPEN: Stormont Estate, Titanic Slipways and Ebrington Square (Derry) all host large outdoor events but no capacity figure was found on any page fetched, so none is recorded; a licensed-capacity source (council entertainments-licence register) would settle them and Belfast City Council does not publish one online.

alternative_names: King's Hall Exhibition and Conference Centre
venues.scale_description: No capacity figure was stated on any page fetched, so none is recorded. What is evidenced: the King's Hall complex comprised 6 event venues on the RUAS's 32-acre Balmoral site; the main hall was designed by Leitch and Partners and opened by the Duke of Gloucester on 29 May 1934; it "was the largest exhibition venue in Northern Ireland and prior to the completion of the Odyssey and the Waterfront Hall, was the only large concert venue in Northern Ireland"; it hosted the Balmoral Show ("regular attendees in excess of 75,000"), the 2003 Special Olympics World Summer Games roller skating, and major professional boxing (Barry McGuigan, Tyson Fury, Amir Khan, Wayne McCullough). RUAS moved out and the building closed to events on 30 June 2012, replaced by Balmoral Park / the Eikon Exhibition Centre in Lisburn. The site is now the £100m King's Hall Health and Wellbeing Park; the developer's site refers to the building's entertainment and boxing history in the past tense, and the listed hall itself is being converted to healthcare use.
venues.no_public_calendar_reason: Closed as an event venue since 30 June 2012 and being redeveloped as a health and wellbeing park; the current site (kings-hall.com) is a property development site with no event programme.

evidence.note: Gives address Lisburn Road, Belfast BT9 6GW; owner Royal Ulster Agricultural Society; opened 30 June 1896 (main hall 1934), closed 30 June 2012; "The King's Hall consisted of 6 event venues"; "The King's Hall was the largest exhibition venue in Northern Ireland and prior to the completion of the Odyssey and the Waterfront Hall, was the only large concert venue in Northern Ireland"; Balmoral Show attendance "in excess of 75,000"; replacement by Balmoral Park and the Eikon Exhibition Centre. No capacity figure is given anywhere in the article.

Current owner/developer site. Confirms the site is now the "Kings Hall Health and Wellbeing Park", a £100m mixed-use scheme, and refers to the venue's entertainment and boxing history in the past tense - i.e. it is no longer an operating event venue.

Royal Ulster Agricultural Society official page. Confirms "The King's Hall was home to the Society for over 75 years" and that the Society has moved to Balmoral Park, "Northern Ireland's largest events campus".

venues.scale_description: Belfast's largest-scale outdoor concert site, owned by Belfast City Council. NO FIXED CAPACITY EXISTS: the Council's own licensing report records the special condition that "Maximum numbers will be agreed at the discretion of the Building Control Service and will vary depending upon individual concert set up proposals", so no capacity value is recorded here. The site "has been used to provide large outdoor concerts for approximately 10 years" and holds both a 14-Day Occasional Outdoor Entertainments Licence and a 14-Day Marquee Entertainments Licence; licensed hours are 11.30am-11.00pm Monday to Saturday and 12.30pm-11.00pm Sunday. Evidenced events at the site include the Ed Sheeran concert of 12 May 2022 and the AVA concerts of 24-25 September 2021. Outdoor venue, and a playing-fields site whose major-event use is non-sport concerts - included as OTHER_MAJOR_EVENT_VENUE and flagged for review.
venues.no_public_calendar_reason: Council-owned open space with no first-party venue site or what's-on page; events are promoted individually by promoters under lease and licence from Belfast City Council, so there is no single publicly accessible first-party event calendar for the venue.

evidence.note: Belfast City Council Licensing Committee report, 15 June 2022, on renewal of the 14-Day Occasional Outdoor Entertainments Licence. Gives the address "Boucher Road Playing Fields, Boucher Road, Belfast, BT12 6EU" and applicant "City and Neighbourhoods Services Dept, Belfast City Council"; states "Boucher Road Playing Fields has been used to provide large outdoor concerts for approximately 10 years" and "is owned by Belfast City Council and currently holds both a 14-Day Occasional Outdoor Entertainments Licence and a 14-Day Marquee Entertainments Licence"; sets out licensed hours; and records the special condition "Maximum numbers will be agreed at the discretion of the Building Control Service and will vary depending upon individual concert set up proposals" - the reason capacity_value is null. Also references the Ed Sheeran concert of 12 May 2022 and the AVA concerts of 24-25 September 2021.
